Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Novacorp pilot: GPU fitment, reserved throughput & SLO MAP

Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a mutual action plan (MAP) to size a short reserved-capacity pilot for your streaming translation workload.

Call highlights (as I heard them)
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end streaming latency target = 150 ms (user-facing, includes token generation).
- Concurrency/throughput: steady-state concurrency expected ~250 concurrent streams, bursts to ~600 for short windows. Average sequence length ~400 tokens; peak seqs up to 2,000 tokens for long sessions.
- Streaming specifics: real-time partial tokens required (server-side chunking), client expects continuous partials every ~200ms. KV cache hits are high (~70%) for repeated user context.
- Data residency: US only for pilot; enterprise production may expand to EU later.

Attachments: I uploaded the quick 1-hour smoke run you shared as CSV logs (novacorp-benchmark-logs.csv) and our draft test plan (laus-testplan.pdf).

Questions / clarifications we need to size the pilot precisely
1) Can you confirm the traffic mix over the pilot window (percent short/medium/long sessions)? A simple split (e.g., 60/30/10) works.
2) Expected sustained tokens/sec per concurrent stream during steady state (roughly).
3) Any hard throughput floor for the pilot PO (minimum reserved qps or tokens/sec)?

Proposed immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Ben: provide GPU-fit recommendation + throughput per GPU estimates by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: draft the pilot commercial (30-day reserved pilot + PO template) and share with your procurement contact.
- Novacorp: confirm traffic mix and procurement lead (Priya we looped on call).

If those look right I’ll put together the MAP and a short test-run checklist (KV warmup, steady-state ramp, burst ramp) and we can lock a kickoff date.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Novacorp pilot: GPU fitment, reserved throughput & SLO MAP

Folks — quick technical sizing based on the traffic mix Sam provided and the latency SLO (p95 <= 150ms for streaming). Assumptions: model variant = open-llama-70b-quant, 8k context for long sessions, KV cache hit = 70%, OSS optimized kernel path.

High-level recommendation (pilot):
- Preferred GPU: NVIDIA H100 (8x H100 equivalent pool) for predictable p95 at scale given streaming requirements.
- Secondary: A100 (40GB) is workable for lower-concurrency pilots but will need increased reserved concurrency and tighter batching to meet 150ms p95.
- Cost/throughput trade: H100 gives ~1.6x throughput vs A100 in our internal streaming benchmarks for this model shape.

Estimated tokens-per-second per GPU (steady-state, warm cache):
- H100 (1 GPU): ~11,000 tokens/sec (conservative)
- A100 (1 GPU): ~6,800 tokens/sec
- L4 (1 GPU): ~2,400 tokens/sec (quantized synthetic only; not recommended for p95 150ms)

Sizing math (back-of-envelope):
- Target steady-state concurrent streams: 250
- Avg tokens/sec per stream (weighted): short 22 * 0.55 + medium 14 * 0.35 + long 8 * 0.10 = ~18.5 tokens/sec per stream
- Total tokens/sec = 250 * 18.5 = ~4,625 tokens/sec
- Conservative headroom (1.8x) for bursts and KV cold-warm transitions = target reserved throughput around 8,325 tokens/sec

Implication:
- H100s required (conservative): ceil(8325 / 11000) = 1 H100 (but we recommend a 2-GPU minimum pool for availability + maintenance windows), so pilot pool = 2 H100s reserved for US region.
- If using A100s, pilot pool = ceil(8325 / 6800) = 2 A100s (recommend 3 for availability).

Pilot test plan notes (short):
- Pre-warm KV cache with a 20-minute ramp and synthetic replay of frequent prefixes.
- Run sustained 60-minute steady-state at 250 concurrency, then a 15-minute burst to 600 concurrency simulating peak.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 and tail token latency; collect token-level traces.

I can formalize these numbers into a short technical appendix for the SOW. Also included a tiny CSV summary (embedded below) and will attach a one-page estimate.

-- Ben
Ben Carter
Performance & Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Duration: 30 days pilot; 14-day technical validation window within pilot.
- Proposed reserved pool (pilot): 2x H100 in US-region (Ben recommended 2 for availability).
- Reserved throughput target: 8,325 tokens/sec (1.8x steady-state headroom).
- Test plan highlights: KV warmup 20m, 60m steady-state @250c, 15m burst @600c, traces + token-level logs.

Owners & deadlines:
- Ben (Redwood) — provide formal appendix and one-page SOW addendum by EOD today.
- Marissa (Redwood) — draft pilot commercial terms & PO template by tomorrow COB.
- Priya (Novacorp) — confirm procurement cadence and send pilot PO within 5 business days once SOW is accepted.
